findings.description: Connections are configured with `cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode = 'quote'`, where backslashes are literal. The new clause emits SQL `ESCAPE '\\'`, a two-character string rather than the single backslash required by LIKE. When MATCH_ALL falls back to `_search_by_like`, even a plain-text query fails instead of returning documents. Emit one SQL backslash for quote mode, or use a bound single-character escape.
findings.failureMode: Every ClickZetta LIKE fallback query uses a two-character ESCAPE string in the configured quote literal mode, causing SQL failure.
findings.title: Use a single-character ESCAPE in ClickZetta quote mode

findings.description: WorkflowRun inputs/outputs are persisted by `json.dumps` with default ASCII escaping. Removing `keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape')` means a search for `你好` now compares literal Unicode against stored `\u4f60\u597d` and returns no logs. JSON-encode the keyword before LIKE-escaping it for these columns; keep a raw-text pattern for EndUser.session_id.
findings.failureMode: Keyword search no longer finds workflow runs containing non-ASCII JSON input/output values.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding in workflow-log searches

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper emits backslash escapes but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. A query such as `50%` therefore looks for a literal backslash followed by a wildcard instead of `50%`, missing matching documents; queries containing `|` also acquire unintended escape semantics. Use the same escape character in both the pattern and SQL.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback searches containing %, _, backslash or | return incorrect results because the SQL escape character differs from the helper's.
findings.title: Match the IRIS escape character to the helper

findings.description: On MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES enabled, NOT LIKE has no default escape character. The pattern for `not contains '50%'` becomes `%50\%%`, so metadata containing `50%` is incorrectly retained because the backslash is literal. Pass `escape='\\'` here, as in the other string-filter branches.
findings.failureMode: Metadata exclusion filters retain documents they should exclude on supported MySQL servers running NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for NOT LIKE too

findings.description: Selecting `Stays in Not Ready` writes the selected event to `expect` and leaves `after` unset. Proactive triggers check absence of `expect`, so the initial Not Ready event satisfies the count, and later silent windows can fire even after the resource has become Ready. In proactive mode put the selected status in `after` and the other statuses in `expect`. The identical binding at work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36 needs the same correction.
findings.failureMode: Both work-pool and work-queue 'Stays in Not Ready' configurations become absence-of-Not-Ready triggers instead of timers that start upon entering and end upon exiting Not Ready.
findings.title: Encode proactive pool and queue status as stay-in triggers

findings.description: Select `Enters Not Ready`, then change to `Stays in` and select `Not Ready` again. The handler now writes `after` but leaves the old `expect: ['prefect.deployment.not-ready']` unchanged. A subsequent Ready event does not match either array, so the proactive trigger fires after the timeout even though the deployment has already recovered. Configure `expect` to the opposite status whenever setting the proactive `after` event; an initially unset expectation also currently matches arbitrary deployment events.
findings.failureMode: A proactive deployment status selection emits after=[selected] without the required complementary expect event, so the timer is satisfied by arbitrary events or stale reactive expectations.
findings.title: Set deployment exit events for proactive status triggers

findings.description: The posture-dependent field name changes which array is edited without clearing the inactive array. After choosing `Stays in Not Ready`, switching to `Enters Ready` leaves `after: ['prefect.deployment.not-ready']` in the trigger. The resulting reactive trigger requires a new Not Ready event before it can respond to Ready, instead of reacting to entering Ready alone. Clear `trigger.after` when switching back to reactive posture.
findings.failureMode: Changing deployment posture from Proactive to Reactive preserves an invisible after condition and suppresses otherwise matching reactive events.
findings.title: Remove the proactive start condition when returning to reactive

findings.description: After entering an event and deleting it, `''.split('\n')` returns `['']`, so this branch stores an empty event name rather than clearing `trigger.expect`. The schema accepts that array, but the backend treats an empty expectation set as any event and a nonempty set containing `''` as matching no real event. Normalize empty/blank input to an empty array or an absent expectation instead.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom-trigger event textarea emits expect: [''] instead of an unconstrained expectation, so a reactive trigger stops matching events.
findings.title: Clear expected events when the textarea is emptied

findings.description: Entering 5 seconds in a new template's proactive Within input passes both this `min={0}` and the wizard schema, but the backend rejects nonzero proactive windows below 10 seconds. Enforce the ten-second minimum in the inputs and proactive schema validation so the wizard cannot emit an invalid trigger. The same input defect occurs at deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:99 and both work-pool/work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:96.
findings.failureMode: The four new templates accept a proactive Within value of 5 seconds that fails backend EventTrigger validation.
findings.title: Enforce the proactive trigger's ten-second minimum

findings.description: A number input accepts scientific notation, but `parseInt('1e2')` returns 1 instead of 100. findings.description: `FormControl` wraps the Radix `Select` root rather than its `SelectTrigger`. The root does not forward the injected ID and ARIA props to the button, so the Status label points at a nonexistent control: `getByLabelText('Status')` fails, clicking the label cannot focus the dropdown, and assistive technology has no field name/error association. It also breaks the existing middleware telemetry assertion. Restore `.available: true` and `default: false`.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode taps send the opposite transition value to telemetry; because the existing wrapper maps isEnabled to isPrivate, previously correctly labelled active normal-mode taps and available private-mode taps are newly mislabelled.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode telemetry transition mapping

findings.description: With Reader View active, `selectedTab.url` is the internal `http://localhost/.../reader-mode/page?url=...` URL, while toolbar state holds the decoded `displayURL`. This predicate now passes the raw reader URL to `cancelEdit`, overriding the display URL. The location view uses that value directly, so Cancel or opening the menu/tab tray changes the displayed article domain to `localhost` and exposes the internal URL when editing again. Restore the reader-URL exclusion so the reducer preserves the existing display URL.
findings.failureMode: Canceling address editing in an active reader tab replaces the article URL with the internal reader URL in toolbar state and display configuration.
findings.title: Preserve the display URL when canceling in Reader View
